Des failles critiques dans PHP et des me: Critical flaws in PHP and immediate precautionary measures
Ce mardi vingt octobre deux mille vingt-: This Tuesday, October twenty, two thousand twenty-six, two critical flaws were identified in the PHP programming language, which powers approximately seventy percent of websites across the globe. This omnipresence combined with an often invisible nature has caused significant difficulties for the global internet, forcing certain organizations to react drastically. Following the example of Orange, entities have chosen to temporarily suspend access to several of their websites and applications as a precautionary measure.
Du côté des acteurs industriels, OpenAI: On the industry side, OpenAI has described this vulnerability discovery as one of the most consequential in recent years, seeing it as the beginning of an unprecedented phase where artificial intelligence succeeds in detecting flaws on an internet-wide scale. Last April, Anthropic had already chosen to restrict public access to its Claude Mythos model, capable of spotting and exploiting such critical flaws.
Jason Clinton, responsable adjoint de la: Jason Clinton, Deputy Chief Information Security Officer at Anthropic, indicates that the situation is expected to continue to worsen before it improves. Expressing his fears on the social network X, he emphasizes that companies must prepare to hold out for about eighteen months in the face of this persistent imbalance between the speed of vulnerability detection by artificial intelligence and the ability of organizations to respond to them.
À terme, les développeurs et les entrepr: Ultimately, developers and companies are expected to intensify the use of artificial intelligence to spot flaws as early as the software design phase and apply patches more quickly.
